known_gaps.privilege_regression_guard_absent: No merge-time gate can catch removal of the privilege block. CI scratch Postgres has no anon or authenticated roles, so the per-role branch never executes there and the drills stay green; Live Schema Parity compares schema shape, not function ACLs. The in-migration assertion is the real control and fires at apply time against a real Supabase. Closing this needs a test asserting the migration still revokes from PUBLIC, anon, and authenticated — the target file is already in file_scope_lock, but adding it moves the anchor again. Flagged for PM decision, not decided unilaterally. See verification.md known gap 4.

anchor_history.reason: Security review found the SECURITY DEFINER helper function carried an implicit PUBLIC EXECUTE grant.

REVOKE ... FROM PUBLIC only. Insufficient on Supabase: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES grant EXECUTE to anon and authenticated as explicit ACL entries, so anon retained EXECUTE. All four CI receipts passed at this head and were still wrong; the gap was found by reading pg_proc.proacl on staging.
Per-role REVOKE (PUBLIC, anon, authenticated) guarded on role existence, with a fail-closed assertion across all three. Proven and mutation-tested on staging.
